corporation organized underthe laws ofthe State of Wyoming("City"), and 19" and Converse LLC,
a Colorado limited liability company, acting by and through its authorized representatives (*"the
Bauers") as follows:

at the intersection formed by Converse Avenue, Pershing Boulevard, and 19rh Street, whichis owned

the City of Cheyenne. This parcel is referred to herein as the“site;”and
WHEREAS, the City filed an eminent domain action(Civil Action No.179-432, First

way; the manner in which traffic will circulate in and out of said access points; the relocation of

building to connect the east and west parking areas on the site; the City's obligation to grade, pave,

1.Following the re-construction ofthe Converse/Pershing/19th Street intersections, and
following the completion of construction of on-site improvements as provided by the October 26,
2012 Stipulation, the City will, at its expense, cause a site plan to be prepared that shall depict and

2.The Bauers shall be entitled to use the site under the Baseline Site Plan for so long
as the site and the existing building are used for any use which is classified as permitted by right
(i.e., uses designated as “P"in Table 5.1 of the UDC). The Bauers shall not be entitled to use the
site for any use which is allowed after administrative review (uses designated as“A"” in Table 5.1
of the UDC) or for any use which is allowed after conditional discretionary review and approval
(uses designated as“C"in Table 5.1 of the UDC) without complying with the review and approval
procedures for such uses specified in the UDC.
3.The Bauers will be required to submit a new site plan, pursuant to the requirements
of the Unified Development Code of the City of Cheyenne ("UDC"), only if:(1) the existing
building is intentionally demolished and a new building is erected on the site; or (2) the Bauers
construct an addition or additions to the existing building which, singly orin combination, expand
the square footage of the existing building, as shown on the Baseline Site Plan, by more than ten
percent (10%).Ifthe existing building is destroyed byfire or other casualty and rebuilt on the same
or substantially similar footprint, no new site plan will be required.For the purposes of this
Agreement, the phrase“substantially similar footprint”shall mean that the total length of the
perimeter of the new building does not exceed the total length of the perimeter of the existing
building by more than ten percent (10%) and that the footprint of the new building occupies at least
ninety percent (90%) of the footprint of the existing building.
4.Inthe eventthe Bauers intentionally demolish theexisting building and erectanynew
building on the site, the Bauers will be required to submit a new site plan which shall comply in all
respects with the UDC without modification.
5.In the event the Bauers construct an addition or additions to the existing building
which, singly orin combination, expand the existing building bymore than ten percent (10%), the
Bauers will be required to submit a new site plan depicting changes from the Baseline Site Plan and
demonstrating compliance with the requirements ofthe UDC relating to setbacks and lot coverage,
exceptthat:

The provisions of UDC Sub-Article 6.2shall not be construed torequire
landscaping which is in addition to the landscaping shown on the Baseline Site Plan; and
b.The provisions of UDC Sub-Article 6.7 will apply only to the addition or
additions to the existing building.
6.In the event the Bauers are required by this Re-Development Agreement to submit
a new site plan, the total number of parking spaces indicated on the Baseline Site Plan and all
parking spaces to be located in the parking lot which will be constructed on the northwest corner of

Circulation. The access points and provisions for circulation of traffic to and from the site, which
provisions are set forth in the Stipulation for Immediate Entry and Possession, filed October 26,
2012, in the above-referenced eminent domain action, shall be deemed to comply in all respects with
UDC, Section 4.3.6., and UDC Sub-Article 6.2. In the event parking requirements associated with
any new use of the site exceed the number of parking spaces to be credited to the site pursuant to
this Section, the Bauers may seek relief from such requirements in accordance with the procedures
provided by the UDC. The Bauers may alter the provisions of the October 26, 2012 Stipulation
relating to access and circulation in accordance with standards and procedures established by the
UDC.
8.The provisions of UDC Section 6.3.5 pertaining to screening and buffering along
common property lines and alleys shall apply regardless of the involuntary taking of right-of-way
needed forthe re-construction ofthe Converse/Pershing/19th Street intersections because the taking
has not resulted in any alteration of said common property lines or alleys.
9.The requirements of UDC Sub-Article 6.4 and UDC Sub-Article 6.5 shall apply
regardless of the involuntary taking of right-of-way needed for the reconstruction of the
Converse/Pershing/19th Street intersections.
10.In the event any dispute arises with regard to the meaning or application of this
Agreement, the City and the Bauers shall first attempt to resolve any such dispute pursuant to the
administrative adjustment provisions ofUDC Section 2.3.4.
11.In the event the Bauers acquire land adjacent to the site with the intention of using
said land in connection with uses on the site, the re-development ofthe adjacent land shallbe subject
to the UDC without modification. In addition, ifit becomes necessary to make modifications to the
site tomake the adjacent land usable in connection with uses on the site, any such modifications of
the site shall be subject to the UDC unless such requirements are modified pursuant to the provisions
of the U DC which relate to variances.
12.The entitlements created by this Agreement shall inure to the benefit of the Bauers
use the existing building(or, pursuant to Section3of this Agreement, a replacement building in the
event the existing building is destroyed byfire or other casualty)for any use permitted or allowed
in the MUB zone pursuant to the requirements and procedures of the UDC.
13.Except to the extent provided by this Re-Development Agreement, the provisions of
the UDC shall remain fully applicable to future development activities and uses of the site. Future
amendments to theUDC shallalso be fully applicable to future development and activities and uses
ofthe site, except that future amendments to the UDC shall not beconstrued to alter the substantive
rights and obligations of the parties under this Re-Development Agreement.

SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT
This Settlement Agreement ("Agreement")is made and entered into by and between
the City of Cheyenne, a municipal corporation organized under thelaws of the State of
Wyoming,("City"),19" and Converse LLC, a Colorado limited liability company ("19" and
Converse LLC"), and Marlene Bauer and Daniel Bauer (collectively,“the Bauers").
RECITALS:
WHEREAS, this Agreement pertains to that certain parcel of real property generally
located at the intersection formed by Converse Avenue, Pershing Boulevard, and 19rh Street,
which is owned by 19"h and Converse LLC and which is legally described as Lots 1, 2, 3 and
4, Ruth Addition to the City of Cheyenne. This parcel is referred to herein as the “Site;”and
WHEREAS, the City filed aneminent domain action(Civil Action No.179-432, First
Judicial District Court, Laramie County, Wyoming)(the “Civil Action")against the Site and
19"h and Converse, LLC, for the purpose of acquiring 9,504 square feet of land (the
"Property")needed for right-of-wayfor there-construction of the Converse Avenue/Pershing
Boulevard/19th Street intersections located immediately east of and adjacent tothe Site(the
"Project"); and
WHEREAS, the parties entered into a partial settlement of the issues in the Civil
Action whichis reflected in a Stipulation for Immediate Entry and Possession which was filed
on October26,2012; and
WHEREAS, the October26,2012Stipulation, inaddition to granting immediate entry,
contemplated that the parties were to negotiate terms and conditions of a“Development
Agreement” to provide certainty to 19h and Converse LLC, and the Bauers, with respect to
regulatory compliance in the event 19ih and Converse LLC, or the Bauers, wish to re-develop
the Site; and
WHEREAS, the City, 19"h and Converse LLC, and the Bauers have now agreed to
certain terms and conditions of a“Re-Development Agreement”and, in addition, wish to
resolve all other matters relating to the Site, the Project, compensation for the acquisition of
the Property, the Civil Action, and any and all other claims, counterclaims, issues and causes
of action that were or could have been included in the Civil Action.
THEREFORE, IN CONSIDERATION OF THE ABOVE RECITALS, MUTUAL
COVENANTS, BENEFITS AND CONSIDERATION PROVIDED EACH TO THE
OTHER, THE PARTIES MUTUALLY COVENANT AND AGREE AS FOLLOWS:
1.The City shall continue to have the right of entry and possession of the Property,
as provided in the Order Permitting Immediate Entry entered in theabove-referenced eminent
domain action, to proceed with and to complete the Project, including construction of a
3:
modern roundabout toreplace the existing Converse Avenue/Pershing Boulevard/19th Street
intersections in Cheyenne, Wyoming, and all related temporary construction easements for
construction, improvements and reclamation related to the Project which are granted by the
Bauers and 19th and ConverseLLC.19"h and ConverseLLC, and the Bauers, agree to execute
such temporary construction easements and other similar documents as may be reasonably
requested by the City for the purposes of implementing the terms and conditions of this
Settlement Agreement.
2.At closing,19" and Converse LLC shall execute and deliver a Warranty Deed
in the form attached hereto as Exhibit 1.At closing, the City shall issue a check in the amount
of Four Hundred Thousand Dollars($400,000.00)drawn on the accounts ofthe City and made
payable to 19"h and Converse LLC.19"h and Converse LLC shall, at its expense, purchase
minimum value title insurance to insure the City's titleto the Property from a title insurance
company authorized to do business in the State of Wyoming.19"and ConverseLLC, shall
cause a commitment for theissuance of said title insurance policy tobeissued to the City at
least ten (10) business days prior to the date for closing of the transaction specified in this
Section of this Settlement Agreement. Closing shall take place on or before July 31, 2013.
Following closing, the City shall have theright to immediately record said Warranty Deed in
the books and records of the Laramie County Clerk and ex-officio register of deeds.
3.In addition to compensation in the amount of Four Hundred Thousand Dollars
($400,000.00) to be paid by the City to 19th and Converse LLC, the City shall provide the
following real property, improvements and benefits, as specified herein, to19'h and Converse
LLC:
a.The City shall grade, pave, stripe, and block two lots located immediately
to thenorth ofthe Site, across Pershing Boulevard, legally described as Lots 30 and 31,
Block One, Eastridge Addition to the City of Cheyenne, in accordance with the
requirements of the Unified Development Code("UDC")and other applicable
provisions of the Cheyenne City Code.The City will also landscape and provide
buffering for these lots in accordance with the UDC, and other applicable provisions
of the Cheyenne City Code, during the Spring of 2014 as weather conditions permit.
It is mutually understood and agreed that these parking lot improvements will be
constructed by Simon Contractors pursuant toits contract with the City to construct the
roundabout described herein. It is also mutually understood and agreed that the City
will not grant final acceptance of these parking lot improvements until all requirements
for landscaping and buffering have been fulfilled by Simon Contractors.In the event,
the Bauers wish to use Lots 30 and31for parking lot purposes prior tofinal acceptance
of the improvements to said lots to be constructed by Simon Contractors, the City and
the Bauers will enterinto a separate lease agreement for said purposes.
b.Within ten (10) business days after completion and acceptance of the
parking lot improvements described in subsection a.of this Section, the City shall
convey Lots 30 and 31, Block One, Eastridge Addition, to 19" and Converse LLC, and
to the Bauers, by Warranty Deed, in the form attached hereto as Exhibit 2.The City

standard, reasonable and necessary specifications, or the construction of a drive aisle
to provide one-way traffic movement from the east parking area to the west parking
